pr_body:
fixes https://github.com/hashicorp/vagrant/issues/11414

Putting this up as an idea. Not sure if I really like the implementation. A couple of questions:
- should vagrant just throw out the whole output when the `--quiet` flag is used?
- are there any instances where the output should be "quiet" but there still needs to be information returned to the user?
- should the `--quiet` flag exist globally, or does it make sense for only some commands to have a quiet option

issue_context.title: vagrant up has not option to silence progress
issue_context.body:
Most CLI tools know to avoid printing progress information when running on non-interactive consoles (no-tty), or at least have an option to disable this.

Apparently there is not cli option for making `vagrant up` less verbose.

### Vagrant version
```
2.2.7
```


### Expected behavior
Be able to control verbosity, especially around progressive commands (those that rewrite current line).


### Actual behavior
```
[K==> default: Successfully added box 'generic/alpine310' (v2.0.6) for 'libvirt'!
2020-02-24 20:28:59.624663 | fedora-30 | ==> default: Uploading base box image as volume into libvirt storage...
2020-02-24 20:29:00.479456 | fedora-30 | 
[KProgress: 0%
[KProgress: 0%

[KProgress: 1%
[KProgress: 1%
[KProgress: 2%
[KProgress: 2%
[KProgress: 2%
[KProgress: 2%

```
### Steps to reproduce
```
vagran up
```

review_comments: Won't need this with dedicated subclass.

Should include a no-op `rewriting` method. 

The `clear_line` method should probably also be overridden. I think the correct behavior would be throwing an error when used, but that would likely introduce unexpected breakages simply for correctness. Might be better to just emit a warning for now, and output a newline instead?

Sounds good. 
When outputting a new line the result of `vagrant up box` is 
```
...
==> vbox: Loading metadata for box 'bento/ubuntu-18.04'
    vbox: URL: https://vagrantcloud.com/bento/ubuntu-18.04
==> vbox: Adding box 'bento/ubuntu-18.04' (v202002.14.0) for provider: virtualbox
    vbox: Downloading: https://vagrantcloud.com/bento/boxes/ubuntu-18.04/versions/202002.14.0/providers/virtualbox.box

    vbox: Download redirected to host: vagrantcloud-files-production.s3.amazonaws.com
...
```


When not outputting a new line the result of `vagrant up box` is 
```
...
==> vbox: Loading metadata for box 'bento/ubuntu-18.04'
    vbox: URL: https://vagrantcloud.com/bento/ubuntu-18.04
==> vbox: Adding box 'bento/ubuntu-18.04' (v202002.14.0) for provider: virtualbox
    vbox: Downloading: https://vagrantcloud.com/bento/boxes/ubuntu-18.04/versions/202002.14.0/providers/virtualbox.box
==> vbox: Box download is resuming from prior download progress
    vbox: Download redirected to host: vagrantcloud-files-production.s3.amazonaws.com
...
```

I think outputting a new line looks a little more messy. But I'm happy to keep it in if you think it's useful for users to see that

I agree, it does look messy, but I think that might be the result of `clear_line` not being used correctly in that location. Generally, when it is used, a line is written without a new line attached so the cursor stays on the line. The clear line will remove the content and return the cursor to the start of the line and then write again. If progress output, or some other type of dynamically modified output, is being displayed and is not wrapped with the `rewriting` method, the result will be one extremely long line. So I think the behavior of writing a new line is okay here, but we'll need to cleanup the clear_line usage internally.
Would you please add a documentation block for this method including a brief explanation of its purpose.
